question: Which permissions can administrators assign to Delegated Developers? (select 2)

options.label: C
options.text: Define coalesce field during a table import

options.label: D
options.text: Setup ACL for the application tables

explanation:
For a specific scoped application, delegated developers can be granted the Delete Application permission and the Manage ACLs & Roles permission. The latter provides access to security-related application files, including access controls for the application's tables. Delegated-developer permissions are available only for scoped applications, not global applications.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Developer and deployment permissions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/delegated-development-and-deployment/developer-permissions.html) · [ServiceNow: Delegate permissions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/delegated-development-and-deployment/t_AddADeveloper.html)

question: One use of the ServiceNow REST API Explorer is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Practice using REST to interact with public data providers

options.label: B
options.text: Find resources on the web for learning about REST

options.label: C
options.text: Convert SOAP Message functions to REST methods

options.label: D
options.text: Create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow

explanation: ServiceNow REST API Explorer can generate sample code for REST requests sent to a ServiceNow instance.

question: It is a best practice to define the business requirements and the process(es) an application will manage within the application development plan. What are some considerations to document as part of the business process?

options.label: A
options.text: Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps

options.label: B
options.text: Business problem, data input/output, project schedule, and process steps

options.label: C
options.text: Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and database capacity

options.label: D
options.text: Business problem, users/stakeholders, available licenses, and database capacity

explanation: A business process should document the business problem, the required data inputs and outputs, the users and stakeholders involved, and the process steps. These describe the process’s purpose, information flow, participants, and workflow; project schedules, license availability, and database capacity are not core business-process documentation elements.

question: Which ATF test step lets you create a user with specified roles and groups for the test?
explanation:
The **Create a User** ATF test step creates a test user with the required roles and group memberships. ServiceNow recommends this approach instead of impersonating an existing user, and rolls back the created test data after the test completes.

**Learn more:** [Automated Test Framework design considerations](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/automated-test-framework-design-considerations.html?contentId=ZCUYsKUmur8iHQFqiyHphQ)

question: Which of the following statements are true about reports in ServiceNow? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Any user can see any report shared with them.

options.label: B
options.text: Can be a graphical representation of data.

options.label: C
options.text: All users can generate reports on any table.

options.label: D
options.text: Can be run on demand by authorized users.

options.label: E
options.text: Can be scheduled to be run and distributed by email.

explanation:
ServiceNow reports visualize current instance data, can be run to view current data by users with the appropriate reporting access, and can be scheduled for distribution by email. Access is role- and permission-dependent, and reporting is not available to every user on every table.

**Learn more:** [Exploring reporting](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/exploring-reporting.html) · [Generate and distribute a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/schedule-report.html?contentId=Cd5ev3Ni6TIcPdyJfPHvzQ)

question: What is the main purpose of an application scope?

options.label: A
options.text: To allow one application to automatically update another’s resources without restrictions

options.label: B
options.text: To control the user interface design for an application

options.label: C
options.text: To define the boundary that isolates an application’s resources from others

options.label: D
options.text: To manage the data storage and backup for applications

explanation:
An application scope establishes an isolation boundary around an application's files, data, and other resources. Other applications cannot access or modify those resources unless explicitly permitted through cross-scope access controls.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html)

question:
What benefits result from storing most of an Application’s server-side script logic in a Script Include?

a. This makes execution faster.
b. The logic only runs when called from a script.
c. The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store.
d. For some changes to application logic there is only one place to make edits.
explanation:
Script Includes store reusable server-side functions and classes. They are loaded only on request, so their logic runs only when another script calls it (b). A Script Include with the Protected protection policy hides its script from customers who install the application, which protects the developer's intellectual property (c). Because the shared logic is defined once and called from many scripts, a change to that logic is made in a single place (d). Storing logic in a Script Include is a matter of organization and reuse; it does not by itself make the code execute faster (a).

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Script includes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_ScriptIncludes.html)

question: When creating a scoped application that includes flow actions, what is that application called?
explanation: A spoke is a scoped application that contains reusable Flow Designer actions and integration-related content.

question: How can a user make further changes after an update set has been marked complete?

options.label: A
options.text: Modify the completed update set directly

options.label: B
options.text: Delete the completed update set and start over

options.label: C
options.text: Revert the update set to "In progress" and add the changes

options.label: D
options.text: Create a new update set for the additional changes

explanation: A completed ServiceNow update set cannot capture additional changes. Further work must be captured in a new update set.

question: What are the benefits of developing private, scoped applications? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab

options.label: B
options.text: To reduce risk at code collisions

options.label: C
options.text: To enable installation and uninstallation of an application

options.label: D
options.text: To replicate ServiceNow functions a private scope

explanation:
A private application scope gives application artifacts a unique namespace, which prevents naming and code collisions. Scoped applications are packaged as a cohesive application, enabling them to be installed and uninstalled as an application.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [ServiceNow: Roll back, back out, and uninstall](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/servicenow-studio/tips-rollback-backout-uninstall.html?contentId=pijf~pd6~Wvd40x1sRT1WQ)

question:
Assume that a table named `table` exists and has three fields: `field1`, `field2`, and `field3`. Review the Access Control list for `table`:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783823862955-5nywbpd8.png)

Which field or fields may a user with the `itil` role read?
explanation:
A user must pass the table ACL and the applicable field ACL. The `itil` role passes the `table.None` read ACL, but does not pass the more specific `table.field3` read ACL because that ACL requires the `admin` role. Thus, the user can read `field1` and `field2`, but not `field3`.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: What is the ServiceNow Application Repository?

options.label: A
options.text: A database containing custom ServiceNow applications

options.label: B
options.text: A database for tracking user permissions

options.label: C
options.text: A database of ServiceNow provided applications

options.label: D
options.text: A database for logging application errors

explanation: The ServiceNow Application Repository stores custom ServiceNow applications so they can be published, versioned, and installed on other instances.

question: What determines the relationships between fields in an Import Set table and fields in an existing ServiceNow table?
explanation:
A Transform Map defines the data relationships between an Import Set table and a target ServiceNow table through its field maps. It specifies how source fields are mapped and transformed into destination fields.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Transform maps](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_CreatingNewTransformMaps.html)

question: Which objects are available for use in Inbound Action scripts?
explanation:
Inbound email action scripts provide the `current` object for the record associated with the inbound email and the `email` object for the current inbound email. `previous` and `producer` are not available inbound-action script objects.

**Learn more:** [Create an inbound email action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreatingAnInboundEmailAction.html)

question: Which of the following is **not** supported by Flow Designer?

options.label: A
options.text: Call a subflow from a flow

options.label: D
options.text: Run a flow from a MetricBase Trigger

explanation:
Flow Designer supports reusable subflows, delegated-developer access, and MetricBase-triggered flows. Testing a flow runs its actions against instance data; it does not include a rollback mechanism to undo the changes made by the test.

**Learn more:** [Building subflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/concept/subflows.html) · [Build your first flow in Workflow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/task/build-your-first-flow.html)

question: Which of the following client-side scripts applies to Record Producers?

options.label: A
options.text: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies

options.label: C
options.text: UI Scripts and Record Producer Scripts

explanation:
A record producer is a type of Service Catalog item. Its form supports associated Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies, which control client-side behavior for its variables and form presentation.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Catalog Item form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-item-form.html) · [ServiceNow: Create a Service Catalog client script](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateACatalogClientScript.html)

question: How should Application Access be configured to stop all other private application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables?

options.label: A
options.text: You must create Access Controls to prevent all other application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables rather than using Application Access

options.label: B
options.text: Set the Accessible from field value to All application scopes and de-select the Can create option

options.label: C
options.text: Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only and de-select the Allow access to this table via web services option

options.label: D
options.text: Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only

explanation:
Design-time Application Access controls whether other application scopes can create configuration records that extend an application's data tables. Restricting **Accessible from** to **This application scope only** denies that design-time access to all other private scopes. The **Can create** option instead controls runtime creation of data records, not configuration records.

**Learn more:** [Design-time access to application tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_DesignTimeAccessToAppTables.html) · [Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question: When designing and creating a form, what do you create to organize fields on the form?
explanation: Sections group and organize related fields within a form.

question: Where can an application be published in ServiceNow once it is ready to be shared? (select 3)

options.label: F
options.text: Publish to a local USB device

explanation:
ServiceNow application-sharing methods include publishing to the application repository for instances in the same company, publishing to the ServiceNow Store for other ServiceNow customers, and publishing to an Update Set for instances that can access the Update Set file.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Application sharing](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/9Lur8HBNLjdzEcjznSAFzA/oDAcZF~U_e_mQ2gUBTbCAw) · [ServiceNow — Developer and deployment permissions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/delegated-development-and-deployment/developer-permissions.html)

question: Which Flow Designer variable data types are supported for storing record data and complex data? (select 3)
explanation:
Per the ServiceNow CAD material, the Flow Designer variable data types supported for storing record and complex data among these options are Integer (B), Array.Reference (C), and String (E). Array.Reference stores a collection of record references (complex/record data), while Integer and String are the supported primitive value types listed. "Label" (A) is not a flow variable data type, and "Choice" (D) is not one of the three in the keyed answer. This matches both the official flow-variable documentation and multiple CAD answer keys.

**Learn more:** [Flow variables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/concept/flow-variables.html)

question: Which class is **not** included in the client-side scoped APIs?
explanation:
The client-side GlideRecord API is not supported in scoped applications. Database access from scoped client scripts should instead use a client-callable Script Include through GlideAjax (or an appropriate REST API).

**Learn more:** [GlideRecord - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideRecordClientSideAPI.html) · [GlideAjax - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideAjaxAPI.html)

question: Which of the following objects can a Before Business Rule access in a script?
explanation:
A Before Business Rule can use the `current` record and, on update or delete operations, the `previous` record. Both are GlideRecord-based record objects, and server-side Business Rule scripts can also create and use `GlideRecord` instances to access other records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/pt-BR/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html) · [ServiceNow GlideRecord API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideRecordAPI.html)

question: When configuring a REST Message, which syntax denotes passing a variable during a function call?
explanation:
Outbound ServiceNow REST messages use `${variable_name}` for variable substitution; the REST message replaces the token with the parameter value when the method executes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Variable substitution in outbound REST messages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/web-services/c_VariableSubstitutionREST.html)

question: Which of the following is **not** a Flow Designer feature?

options.label: A
options.text: Run a flow from a Catalog item

options.label: B
options.text: Call a flow from another flow or subflow

options.label: D
options.text: Test a flow using the “Run as” feature

explanation:
The **Run As** property sets the identity under which a flow executes—either the system user or the user who initiated the session. Flow testing runs a saved flow with supplied test data; Run As is not a test-as-user feature. Flow Designer does support Service Catalog-triggered flows and stages.

**Learn more:** [Build flows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flows.html) · [Create a flow with a Service Catalog trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/task/create-sc-flow.html)

question: Which UX format is best suited for lists and forms?
explanation: The Classic UX format supports both list and form interfaces, making it the appropriate format when an experience requires both types of record interaction.

question: Which feature provides a graphical view of the relationships between tables in ServiceNow?
explanation:
A Schema Map visually displays tables and their relationships, including referenced-by, referencing, extended-by, and extending relationships.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Viewing table references and extensions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/c_SchemaMapForTables.html)

question: What is one function of an update set in ServiceNow Studio?

options.label: A
options.text: To track and monitor system performance metrics

options.label: C
options.text: To manage configurations directly in a production environment

options.label: D
options.text: To group configuration changes for transfer between instances

explanation: An update set groups configuration changes so they can be transferred from one ServiceNow instance to another.

question: When creating a SOAP Message, which syntax identifies a variable to be passed when the function is called?
explanation:
ServiceNow outbound SOAP variable substitution uses the `${variable_name}` format, allowing the variable’s value to be supplied for the SOAP Message Function when it runs.

**Learn more:** [Variable substitution in outbound SOAP](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/web-services/c_VariableSubstitutionSOAP.html)

question: Which of the following statements must evaluate to true for a user to pass an Access Control? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: The user has one of the roles specified in the Required roles related list.

options.label: B
options.text: Scripts configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.

options.label: C
options.text: Other matching Access Controls for the records evaluate to true.

options.label: D
options.text: Conditions configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.

options.label: E
options.text: The user must be granted access through a business rule.

explanation:
An Access Control rule grants access only when its required-role check passes, its configured condition evaluates to true, and its configured script evaluates or returns true. A Business Rule does not grant Access Control permission. [ServiceNow: Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: Which methods can be used to install an application on a ServiceNow instance? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Install from the Google Play Store.

options.label: C
options.text: Download and install a third-party application from the ServiceNow Store.

options.label: D
options.text: Use the "Install" button on the application record.

options.label: E
options.text: Install an application from the Application Repository.

options.label: F
options.text: Import an application from an XML file.

explanation: ServiceNow supports installing applications obtained from the ServiceNow Store, initiating installation with the **Install** button on an application record, and installing applications that have been published to the Application Repository. These are ServiceNow-supported application distribution and installation mechanisms.

question: Which records track cross-scope applications or scripts that request access to an application, application resource, or event?
explanation:
Restricted Caller Access records track requests by cross-scope applications or scripts to access an application, an application resource, or an event. These records support allowing, denying, and tracking such requests.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Restricted caller access privilege settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/restricted-caller-access-privilege.html)

question: Which feature can be used to add instructions to a form?

options.label: A
options.text: A Context Menu UI Action for instructions

explanation: Annotations display instructional text directly on a form for users.

question: Which of the following statements about the Form Designer is **NOT** true?

options.label: A
options.text: To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab to the desired destination on the form.

options.label: B
options.text: To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the Fields tab to the desired destination on the form.

options.label: C
options.text: To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, and select the Delete (X) button.

options.label: D
options.text: To create a new field on a form’s table, drag the appropriate data type from the Field Types tab to the form and then configure the new field.

explanation:
In ServiceNow Form Designer, a new section is created with the (+) button beside an existing section’s label; sections can subsequently be dragged to reorder them. The Field Types tab is used for field types, including creating new fields on the selected table when the layout is saved.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

question: Can an application's scope be changed?

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, but only from global scope to private scope

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, but only from private scope to global scope

explanation:
In ServiceNow, an application scope is the application's unique namespace and access-protection boundary, selected when the application is created. It cannot be changed for an existing application; selecting another scope only changes the active development context.

**Learn more:** [Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [Plan before you build](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/plan-before-you-build.html)

question: Which server-side API method for debug logging is available in scoped applications?
explanation:
The scoped GlideSystem API includes `gs.info()` to write informational log messages from server-side code. `gs.log()` and `gs.print()` are not available in scoped applications, and `gs.debuglog()` is not a valid GlideSystem method.

**Learn more:** [GlideSystem - Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemScopedAPI.html)

question: Which scoped application includes Flow Designer actions tailored to a specific application or record type?
explanation:
A ServiceNow spoke is a scoped application that packages Flow Designer content, including actions, for a particular application or record type.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Spokes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/concept/spokes.html)

question: When assessing Access Controls, ServiceNow searches for and evaluates:

options.label: A
options.text: Only for matches on the current table

options.label: B
options.text: Only for matches on the current field

options.label: C
options.text: From the most specific match to the most generic match

options.label: D
options.text: From the most generic match to the most specific match

explanation:
ServiceNow Access Control List (ACL) processing uses specific matching rules before broader fallback rules, so an applicable resource is evaluated from the most specific match toward the most generic match.

**Learn more:** [ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: Which capability does Flow Designer support?

options.label: A
options.text: The role flow_operator can create and edit flows.

options.label: B
options.text: Flows can be "Run as” security admin.

options.label: C
options.text: Call a subflow from a flow.

options.label: D
options.text: Flows can trigger off a record being deleted.

explanation:
A flow can invoke a subflow to reuse a defined sequence of actions, inputs, and outputs. ServiceNow documents that subflows can be called from other flows or from scripts.

**Learn more:** [Create a subflow in Workflow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/create-subflow.html)

question: Identify the method(s) by which an application can respond to an event generated by the `gs.eventQueue()` method.
explanation:
ServiceNow event processing can invoke a Script Action or send a notification in response to an event placed in the event queue. UI Policies control client-side form behavior, and Scheduled Script Executions are not event-response handlers. [ServiceNow System Events documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/events.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow System Events](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/events.html) · [ServiceNow Create event](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/t_CreateYourOwnEvent.html)

question: When creating a table in a privately scoped application, which four Access Controls are created for that table?
explanation:
ServiceNow automatically configures Access Controls during table creation so that authorized users can read, create, write, and delete records. A write ACL controls updates to existing records. [ServiceNow Secure data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/secure-data.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Secure data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/secure-data.html) · [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: While using Form Designer, configuring a field label in a child table changes the label on which table(s)?
explanation:
For an inherited field, the label is maintained at the field’s nearest base-table definition. Child tables inherit fields and their associated configuration from parent tables, so configuring that inherited label in Form Designer changes it on the base table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg)

question: Who can see a module when its **Roles** field is blank?

options.label: A
options.text: Users with no attached roles on the user record

options.label: C
options.text: User roles with access to the application menu

explanation:
When a ServiceNow module’s **Roles** field is left blank, the module is visible to every user who can access its parent application menu. The blank field does not limit visibility to users with no roles or specifically to the `snc_internal` role.

**Learn more:** [Application Navigator category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html?contentId=bMdMEmowhugdNysA9r21Cw)

question: Which field type should you select to query records from a different table on a form?

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Phone Number field type.

explanation: A Reference field creates a relationship to another table, enabling a form field to look up and select records from that table.

question: What is needed to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository? (select 3)
explanation:
A Git source-control connection requires the repository URL plus credentials that have read and write access to that repository. With basic authentication, those credentials consist of a user name and password. ServiceNow’s current documentation represents these as a repository URL and a credential record; access tokens are recommended in place of passwords where supported.

**Learn more:** [Link an app to source control in ServiceNow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/link-app-to-source-control.html) · [Source control integration in ServiceNow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/source-control-integration.html)

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Application Picker and Application Scope?

options.label: A
options.text: Global is a reserved application which does not appear in the Application Picker

options.label: B
options.text: Selecting an application from the Application Picker does not set the Application Scope

options.label: C
options.text: Selecting an application from the Application Picker sets the Application Scope

options.label: D
options.text: Selecting Global in the Application Picker sets the Application Scope to Incident

explanation:
The Application Picker selects the current application scope, which determines the scope context for new records and updates. [ServiceNow: Select an application from the application picker](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_SelectAnAppFromTheAppPicker.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Select an application from the application picker](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_SelectAnAppFromTheAppPicker.html)

question: Which of the following is included in the client-side scripting API?
explanation: The GlideUser object, available as `g_user`, is a client-side API that provides information about the currently logged-in user. `gs`, `current`, `previous`, and `workflow.scratchpad` are used in server-side scripting contexts.

question: What are Application Files within a ServiceNow application?

options.label: A
options.text: An XML export of an application's table records

options.label: B
options.text: CSV files containing data imported into an application

options.label: D
options.text: XML exports of an application's Update Set

explanation:
Application files are ServiceNow configuration and metadata artifacts that define application functionality, such as business rules, workflows, and script includes. These configuration records are associated with the application and can be tracked in update sets. [ServiceNow: Application files](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ApplicationFiles.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Documentation: Application files](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ApplicationFiles.html)

question: In a privately scoped application, which methods are used to log messages in server-side scripts? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow’s scoped GlideSystem API provides gs.debug() for debug messages, gs.info() for informational messages, and gs.error() for error messages. The legacy gs.log() and gs.logError() methods are global-API methods and are not available in scoped applications. The scoped logging-method list therefore includes all three applicable methods.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers — Server-side Scripting](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-module&identifier=SSS_About_zurich%2Cservicenow_administrator&module=learning+plan&release=zurich) · [ServiceNow Developers — Debugging Widgets](https://developer.servicenow.com/dev.do?_escaped_fragment_=%2Flearn%2Flearning-plans%2Fxanadu%2Fservicenow_application_developer%2Fapp_store_learnv2_serviceportal_xanadu_debugging_widgets)

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a UI Action type?
explanation:
A UI Action's display options in ServiceNow are Form button, Form context menu, Form link, List banner button, List bottom button, List context menu, List choice, and List link. "List choice" (A), "Form button" (B), and "List banner button" (C) are all valid UI Action types. "Form choice" (D) is NOT a UI Action type - choices exist only in the list group, never on forms. Therefore D is the type that does not exist.

**Learn more:** [UI Actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/list-administration/concept/c_UIActions.html) · [Create a UI action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/list-administration/task/t_EditingAUIAction.html)

question: How is access to application menus and modules governed?
explanation: ServiceNow uses roles assigned to users to determine access to application menus and modules.

question: Which types of scripts run on the server? (select 3)
explanation:
Business Rules are server-side scripts that run in response to database operations. Script Actions are server-side scripts triggered by events. Scheduled Jobs can execute scripts automatically at a specified time or on a recurring schedule. Client Scripts and UI Policies control client-side form behavior in the browser.

**Learn more:** [Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html) · [Script actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/system-events/r_ScriptActions.html)

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding client-side scripted security?

options.label: A
options.text: Client-side scripts have access to both the GlideSystem (gs) and GlideUser (g_user) methods

options.label: B
options.text: Client-side scripts have access to the GlideUser (g_user) methods

options.label: C
options.text: Client-side scripts have no access to user methods

options.label: D
options.text: Client-side scripts have access to the GlideSystem (gs) user methods

explanation:
Client-side scripts can access current-user information and role methods through the client-side GlideUser global object, `g_user`. GlideSystem (`gs`) is server-side and is not available to client scripts.

**Learn more:** [GlideUser - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideUserAPI.html)

question:
Which roles provide access to source-control repository operations, such as importing applications from source control or linking an application to source control?

(select 2)
explanation:
In ServiceNow Studio, both the `admin` and `source_control` roles authorize source-control repository operations, including importing an application from source control and linking an application to a repository.

**Learn more:** [Legacy - Import application or application-customization from source control](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/t_ImportAppFromSourceControl.html?contentId=hdQh1pbvhlu2~IGRzmAvMA) · [ServiceNow Developers — Linking an Application to Source Control](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=course-module&identifier=app_store_learnv2_devenvironment_yokohama_source_control%2Capp_store_learnv2_devenvironment_yokohama_exercise_create_and_link_a_repository&module=course&release=yokohama)

question: Which of these methods, by default, displays a message on a blue background at the top of the current form?
explanation:
`g_form.addInfoMessage()` is the GlideForm client API method for adding an informational message at the top of a form. Informational messages use the default blue presentation; field-message methods display messages associated with an individual field instead.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideForm (g_form) Client API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideFormAPI.html) · [ServiceNow Scripting alert, info, and error messages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/api-reference/scripts/r_ScriptingAlertInfoAndErrorMsgs.html)

question: A module must have a Link type. Which of the following is a list of Link types?

options.label: A
options.text: List of Records, Separator, Catalog Type, Roles

options.label: B
options.text: Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page

options.label: C
options.text: List of Records, Content Page, Order, URL (from arguments:)

options.label: D
options.text: Assessment, List of Records, Content Page, Roles

explanation:
ServiceNow module Link types include Assessment, List of Records, Separator, and Timeline Page. Roles and Order are module fields, while the other listed entries do not make their respective options a list composed entirely of the specified Link types.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Application Navigator category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html?contentId=bMdMEmowhugdNysA9r21Cw)

question:
Which of the following are configured in an Email Notification?

- a) Who receives the notification.
- b) What content the notification includes.
- c) When the notification is sent.
- d) How the notification is sent.
explanation:
ServiceNow email notifications allow administrators to define when to send the notification, who receives it, and the content it contains. “How to send the notification” is not a core email-notification configuration category.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Email and SMS notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_EmailNotifications.html)

question: How does ServiceNow associate an inbound email with an existing record?
explanation: ServiceNow embeds a unique watermark in outbound email messages. When a reply is received, that watermark lets the platform identify and associate the inbound email with the corresponding existing record.

question: Which of the following statements is true about a Script Include whose Protection Policy value is **Protected**?

options.label: A
options.text: Any user with the protected_edit role can see and edit the Script Include

options.label: B
options.text: The Protection policy option can only be enabled by a user with the admin role

options.label: C
options.text: The Protection Policy is applied only if the glide.app.apply_protection system property value is true

options.label: D
options.text: The Protection Policy is applied only if the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store

explanation:
A Protected Script Include is encrypted on instances where its application is installed from the ServiceNow Store, so the protection policy applies to Store-downloaded applications. [ServiceNow Developer learning plan](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-plans&identifier=new_to_servicenow&module=learning+plan&release=yokohama)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developer learning plan](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-plans&identifier=new_to_servicenow&module=learning+plan&release=yokohama)

question: Which of the following features are available for Global applications? (select 2)
explanation:
Automated Test Framework and Flow Designer are platform capabilities that can be used in the global scope. Delegated development is unavailable for globally scoped applications, which lack the application boundaries required for delegated-development controls.

**Learn more:** [Plan before you build — ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/plan-before-you-build.html?contentId=20Lmi4w3SRm1GRRaabOr6g)

question: Application developers can use the Record Producer UI to specify which ServiceNow page a user sees after submitting a new record. How is the page specified?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an application property to store the URL

options.label: B
options.text: Configure the page in the Module that opens the Record Producer UI

options.label: C
options.text: Write an after Business Rule script for the Record Producer's table: window.redirect = "<URL>";

options.label: D
options.text: Write a script in the Record Producer's Script field: producer.redirect = "<URL>";

explanation:
A Record Producer can redirect users after submission by setting `producer.redirect` to the target URL in its Script field. This enables redirect behavior in the Platform UI.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Populate record producer data and redirect users](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_PopulatingRecordData.html)

question: Within a Business Rule, which of the following returns true when the currently logged-in user has the admin role?
explanation: Business Rules run on the server, so role membership for the current user is evaluated with GlideSystem. `gs.hasRole('admin')` returns true when that user has the `admin` role.

question: Which items are valid UI Action types in ServiceNow? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow supports UI Actions such as a button on a form, a button in a list banner, and an item in the action choice list at the bottom of a list. These correspond to Form button, List banner button, and List choice.

**Learn more:** [Create a UI action](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_EditingAUIAction.html) · [UI actions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_UIActions.html?contentId=O5VhPOzlmtsfIWzc3NO23g)

question: Which Application Access configuration field(s) are unavailable when the **Can read** configuration field is not selected?

options.label: A
options.text: All access to this table via web services

options.label: B
options.text: Can create, Can update, and Can delete

options.label: C
options.text: Can read does not affect the availability of other Application Access fields

explanation:
ServiceNow requires read access before granting other cross-scope record operations. Therefore, the create, update, and delete permissions are unavailable until **Can read** is selected.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question: Which of the following is **not** a Caller Access field option?
explanation: ServiceNow provides the Caller Access options **Caller Tracking**, **Caller Restriction**, and **None**. **Caller Permission** is not a valid Caller Access field option.

question: Which objects are available for use in a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) script?
explanation:
Scheduled Script Executions run on the server, where `gs` provides the GlideSystem API and scripts can create `GlideRecord` objects to access table records. Because the job is not executing against a specific record, no `current` record is supplied. ServiceNow’s scheduled-script documentation demonstrates use of both `gs` and `GlideRecord`.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Run a script of your choosing](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/t_ScheduleAScriptExecution.html) · [ServiceNow: GlideSystem API (Global)](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

question: Identify the statement about Delegated Development in ServiceNow that is incorrect.

options.label: A
options.text: Administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications.

options.label: B
options.text: Administrators can specify which application file types the developer can access.

options.label: C
options.text: Administrators can grant the developer access to script fields.

options.label: D
options.text: Administrators can grant the developer access to security records.

explanation:
Delegated Development is available for scoped applications; globally scoped applications cannot use it. Administrators can grant scoped-application permissions for application file types, write access to script fields, and security-related file types such as access controls and user roles.

**Learn more:** [Plan before you build](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/plan-before-you-build.html?contentId=20Lmi4w3SRm1GRRaabOr6g) · [Developer and deployment permissions](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/delegated-development-and-deployment/developer-permissions.html?contentId=RsUOFNB1qp0dxP3x4l6bIw)

question: For what purpose is a `g_scratchpad` object used?

options.label: A
options.text: Populate the properties for Display Business Rule

options.label: B
options.text: Pass the data from server-side to client-side script on Mobile

options.label: C
options.text: Define constructors and destructors for table class

options.label: D
options.text: Pass the data from server-side to client-side script on Web

explanation:
`g_scratchpad` passes data from server-side logic to client-side scripts on a web form. A Display Business Rule can set its properties before the form is delivered, making those values available to client-side scripting when the form loads.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Design and processing](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/client-script-best-practices.html)

question: What is the purpose of the "enforcing" option in Runtime access tracking settings?

options.label: A
options.text: Logs access requests to cross-scope resources and requires an administrator to authorize each request.

options.label: B
options.text: Blocks all access requests to cross scope resources.

options.label: C
options.text: Authorizes all access requests to cross scope resources without logging there.

options.label: D
options.text: Logs and authorizes all access requests to cross-scope resources automatically.

explanation:
The Enforcing setting logs cross-scope access requests and requires an administrator to authorize each one before the requested operation can run.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/zurich/application-development/building-applications/r_ApplicationDesignAndRuntimeSettings.html?contentId=q8PvGE8LdNF9E20IYlg2TQ) · [ServiceNow: Runtime access tracking](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_RuntimeAccessTracking.html?contentId=JQ6FvH~zOpHYBQZn8WEoIA)

question: The source-control operation that stores local changes on an instance for application later is called a(n) <blank>.
explanation: A stash saves local, uncommitted changes temporarily and allows them to be reapplied later without committing them to the current branch.

question: Which of the following statements about `g_scratchpad` are true? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Used to push information from the server to the client

options.label: B
options.text: Does not exist on the mobile platform

options.label: D
options.text: Has default properties passed by client-side scripts

explanation:
`g_scratchpad` is an initially empty object that a display business rule uses to pass name:value data from the server to client-side scripts. It does not provide constructors, methods, or default client-script-supplied properties, and it is not available on the mobile platform.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Classic Business Rules documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

question: An application developer wants to examine the scripts, reports, and other application artifacts that are included in a published application. What steps should be taken to review those items?

options.label: A
options.text: Enter the name of the Application in the Global search field

options.label: B
options.text: Open the list of Update Sets for the instance

options.label: C
options.text: Examine the Application Files Related List in the application to be published

options.label: D
options.text: Open the artifact records individually to verify the value in the Application field

explanation:
ServiceNow application files represent an application’s configuration artifacts, including items such as scripts and reports. The Application Files related list on the custom application record provides the complete list of those artifacts, enabling review before publication.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation: Application files](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ApplicationFiles.html)

question: Which intuitive development interface leads users through the initial application-development process?
explanation: ServiceNow Guided Application Creator provides a guided interface for initiating an application and walking through its initial development setup. It is distinct from ServiceNow Studio, which is a general development environment, Flow Designer for process automation, and Guided Tour Designer for user guidance tours.

question: Which report type(s) can you create by right-clicking a column header in a table list?

options.label: A
options.text: Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Histogram, and Line

options.label: C
options.text: Bar Chart, Pie Chart, and Histogram

explanation:
ServiceNow lets users create a Bar Chart or Pie Chart directly from a platform list by right-clicking an eligible column header. Histogram and Line reports must be created through other reporting workflows. [ServiceNow: View a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/t_RunAReport.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow documentation — View a report](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/now-intelligence/reporting/t_RunAReport.html)

question:
From the list below, identify one reason why an application might **NOT** be a good fit for ServiceNow.

The application:

options.label: B
options.text: Requires ג€as-isג€ use of low-level programming libraries

options.label: D
options.text: Uses forms extensively to interact with data

explanation:
ServiceNow is well suited to applications that use forms, reporting, and workflows to manage business processes. It is not a good fit when the application requires unchanged use of low-level programming libraries, because ServiceNow applications must operate within the platform’s supported development runtime and APIs; libraries that depend on unsupported functionality cannot be used as-is.

**Learn more:** [Use third-party libraries in applications in the ServiceNow IDE](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-ide-family-release/use-third-party-libraries-ide.html)

question: Which Link type creates a module that opens a Record Producer UI rather than a Form UI?
explanation:
A Record Producer is opened through a URL that points to the catalog item view, so the module Link type must be "URL (from Arguments:)", where the Arguments field holds the record-producer URL (e.g. com.glideapp.servicecatalog_cat_item_view.do?sysparm_id=<sys_id>). This produces a module that loads the Record Producer UI instead of a standard Form. "Content Page" is used for CMS/portal content pages, "Script (from Arguments:)" builds the URL via server script for other purposes, and "HTML (from Arguments:)" renders raw HTML — none of these are the standard mechanism for opening a Record Producer.

**Learn more:** [Module link types](https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/rome-platform-user-interface/page/administer/navigation-and-ui/reference/r_ModuleLinkTypes.html) · [Call a record producer from a module link](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/can-you-call-a-record-producer-from-a-module-link-and-have-it/m-p/1645488)

question: How many application menus is an application allowed to have?

options.label: A
options.text: 3, one for an application's user modules, one for an application's administrator modules, and one for the ServiceNow administrator's modules

options.label: B
options.text: As many as the application design requires

options.label: C
options.text: 2, one for an application's user modules and one for an application's administrator modules

options.label: D
options.text: 1, which is used for all application modules

explanation:
A ServiceNow application uses one application menu for all of its modules. Access to individual modules, including administrator-only functionality, is controlled through role restrictions. [Create an application menu](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html)

**Learn more:** [Create an application menu](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html)

question: Which of the following is a recommended practice for adding instructions to a form?
explanation:
Form annotations provide on-screen instructional text and additional information directly within a form, helping users complete it correctly.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Form annotations](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormAnnotation.html?contentId=1vx_xx5QomhV9I4xwYqL0A)

question: How can administrators broaden the list of file types supported for code search in ServiceNow Studio?

options.label: A
options.text: By modifying the default code search table

options.label: C
options.text: By creating a new code search group

options.label: D
options.text: By adding new file types to a custom search group

explanation:
ServiceNow Studio code search uses a default code search group. To expand the supported file types, an administrator creates a new code search group that includes the additional file types; searchable file types must extend the `sys_metadata` table.

**Learn more:** [Supported code search file types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/sn-studio-file-types.html)

question: When troubleshooting Email Notifications, which items must be checked on a user record? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: The First name and Last name fields must have values.

options.label: C
options.text: The value in the Notification field must be set to enabled.

options.label: D
options.text: The user must not be locked out.

options.label: E
options.text: The Email field must have a value.

explanation:
For outbound email notifications, the recipient must have an active user record, notifications enabled on that record, and an email address. ServiceNow does not send a notification to a user with an inactive User record, and it can exclude recipients whose Notification field is set to Disabled.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html) · [Available system properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/r_AvailableSystemProperties.html)

question: For a table that has the `Allow configuration` option selected under Application Access, which statement is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the in scope application's scripts can create Business Rules for the table

options.label: B
options.text: Any user with the application's user role can modify the application's scripts

options.label: C
options.text: Out of scope applications can create Business Rules for the table

options.label: D
options.text: Out of scope applications can add new tables to the scoped application

question: Which options are valid for the Caller Access field? (select 3)
explanation:
ServiceNow defines the Caller Access levels as **None**, **Caller Restriction**, and **Caller Tracking**. None evaluates cross-scope access through the Accessible from setting; Caller Restriction requires manual approval; and Caller Tracking automatically approves while recording the call.

**Learn more:** [Define cross-scope access to an application resource](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/set-RCA-level.html)

question: Which of the following is **not** required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository?
explanation:
A Git repository link uses the repository URL and authentication credentials. The application is selected in ServiceNow Studio, so an application name is not required as a repository connection detail.

**Learn more:** [Link an app to source control in ServiceNow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/link-app-to-source-control.html) · [Connect to a Git provider using basic authentication](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-ide-family-release/connect-git-provider-basic-auth.html)

question: Which database operations can Application Access control? (select 2)
explanation:
Application Access (the settings on a table's dictionary record) controls how records are reached from other application scopes via the Can create, Can read, Can update, and Can delete options — so among the choices, Update (A) and Create (B) are both controllable. Query is the classic exception: it is the database operation that CANNOT be restricted through Application Access, which eliminates C. Execute (D) is not an Application Access database operation at all. Therefore the two controllable operations listed are Create and Update.

**Learn more:** [Access control rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/yokohama-platform-security/page/administer/security-center/reference/sc-access-control.html) · [Which DB operation cannot be controlled with Application Access](https://www.servicenow.com/community/training-and-certifications/what-database-operation-cannot-be-controlled-with-application/m-p/363970)

question: What is the function of the Application Picker?

options.label: B
options.text: Select an application as a favorite in the Application Navigator

options.label: C
options.text: Choose an application to edit and set the Application Scope

options.label: D
options.text: Choose an application to download and install

explanation:
The Application Picker selects the current application scope, which controls the application context in which development changes and new records apply. [ServiceNow: Application picker](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationPicker.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application picker](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationPicker.html)

question: Which Link types are available for assignment to a module in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: List of Records, Content Page, Order, URL (from arguments:)

options.label: B
options.text: List of Records, Separator, Catalog Type, Roles

options.label: C
options.text: Assessment List of Records, Content Page, Roles

options.label: D
options.text: Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page

explanation:
ServiceNow modules support link types including Assessment, List of Records, Separator, and Timeline Page. Roles control access to a module, rather than defining the link it opens.

**Learn more:** [Application Navigator category — Module link types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html?contentId=bMdMEmowhugdNysA9r21Cw) · [Make a timeline visible to a selected user](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/t_MakeATimelineVisibleToASelUser.html)

question: After an application is ready to be shared, which of these publishing methods does ServiceNow support? (select 3)

options.label: F
options.text: Publish to a local USB device

explanation:
ServiceNow applications can be distributed internally through the application repository, shared between instances through Update Sets, or submitted to the ServiceNow Store for broader distribution. ServiceNow Studio supports publishing an application to an Update Set or the application repository, and ServiceNow developer guidance also identifies submitting applications to the ServiceNow App Store.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers — Introduction to Application Development](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=now-platform&identifier=pro-dev-intro&module=guide&release=yokohama)

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a debugging strategy for client-side scripts?
explanation:
Client-side scripts execute in the web browser and can use browser-oriented tools such as the JavaScript Log, Field Watcher, and form messages. `gs.log()` is a server-side GlideSystem logging method, so it is not available as a client-side debugging technique.

**Learn more:** [Writing to the debug log](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_WritingToTheDebugLog.html) · [JavaScript debug window](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_JavaScriptDebugWindow.html?contentId=K6H8yK9UdqtiF8TgZ2fqPg)

question: Can fields inherited by a table be deleted?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, select the red X in the left-most column in the table definition

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, but only if they are text fields

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, but only if there has never been any saved field data

options.label: D
options.text: No, inherited fields cannot be deleted from a child table

explanation: Fields inherited from a parent table cannot be deleted from a child table because their definitions belong to the parent table and are shared through inheritance.

question: What is one reason to build a custom application? (select 2)

options.label: C
options.text: To create a custom integration for a 3rd party system

options.label: D
options.text: To fulfill a specific use case on internal processes

explanation:
Custom applications can fulfill organization-specific internal-process use cases and support bespoke integrations with third-party systems. ServiceNow supports building custom integrations through its platform integration interfaces; custom applications should extend the platform rather than replace base tables.

**Learn more:** [Integration options](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_IntegrationOptions.html) · [Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html)

question: Which of the following objects can a Display Business Rule **not** access?
explanation:
A Display Business Rule executes when a record is read for presentation, so it operates on the current record and can populate `g_scratchpad`; it can also use server-side GlideSystem functionality through `gs`. A `previous` record state is associated with update or delete processing and is not available for a display operation.

**Learn more:** [Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html) · [GlideSystem - Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

question: Which Automated Test Framework (ATF) test step is used to configure a specific user profile?
explanation: The **Impersonation** ATF test step sets the active user context for the test, so subsequent steps run with that specific user's profile, roles, and permissions.

question: Which of these methods is **not** included in the ServiceNow REST API?
explanation:
ServiceNow REST API resources support GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE HTTP methods. COPY is not included in that supported method set.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers — Scripted REST API Resources](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-module&identifier=SRA_Lab_CreateBranch_yokohama%2Cservicenow_application_developer&module=learning+plan&release=yokohama)

question:
Which of the following statements is true about this script fragment?

options.label: D

The GlideUser `hasRole()` method returns true when the current user has the specified role or has the `admin` role.

question: What occurs if a record producer script aborts the record-generation process in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: Record creation displays an error message to the user

options.text: Record is not generated in the Item Produced Record table

options.label: C
options.text: Record creation is redirected to a confirmation page

options.label: D
options.text: Record creation terminates without notifying the user

explanation:
When a record producer script aborts record generation, ServiceNow does not generate an entry in the Item Produced Record (`sc_item_produced_record`) table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Record Producer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/c_RecordProducer.html)

question: Which of the following methods can be used in Access Control scripts?
explanation:
Access Control scripts execute on the server. `gs.hasRole()` checks whether the current user has a role, and `current.isNewRecord()` identifies a record that has not yet been inserted.

**Learn more:** [GlideSystem - Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html) · [GlideRecord - Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideRecordAPI.html)

question: What is one characteristic of Modules?

options.label: A

options.text: Access to Modules is not controlled with roles.

options.label: C
options.text: Every Module must be part of an Application Menu.

options.label: D
options.text: Modules cannot open forms or lists.

ServiceNow modules are child, second-tier navigation options within an application menu. [ServiceNow: Application Navigator category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html?contentId=bMdMEmowhugdNysA9r21Cw)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application Navigator category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html?contentId=bMdMEmowhugdNysA9r21Cw)

question: Which capabilities does Flow Designer provide? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: Call a flow from another flow or subflow.

options.label: C
options.text: Test a flow using the “Run as” feature.

options.label: D
options.text: Support Java Scripting code to test conditions that trigger the flow.

options.label: E
options.text: Run a flow from a Catalog item.

options.label: F
options.text: Perform form field data validation at client side.

explanation:
Flow Designer supports adding stages to flows, reusing automation by calling it from other flows or subflows, and running a flow when an associated Service Catalog item is requested. The **Run as** setting specifies execution context rather than providing a user-selection testing feature. Flow Designer uses declarative conditions and server-side automation, not client-side form validation or JavaScript condition code.

**Learn more:** [Flow and subflow stages](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/flow-designer-stages.html) · [Building subflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/concept/subflows.html)

question: For Application Access, a configuration option is named **Allow access to this table via web services**. Which of the following statements is true when this option is selected?

options.label: D
options.text: The user performing the query via web services must have the correct permissions to access the table's records

explanation:
Selecting this option permits inbound web-service queries to the table, while access controls still apply. A user who queries through web services must have the appropriate permissions to access the table’s records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question: Which object is used for GlideForm client-side scripting?
explanation:
ServiceNow makes GlideForm methods available to client-side scripts through the global `g_form` object, such as `g_form.getValue()` and `g_form.setValue()`.

**Learn more:** [The GlideForm (g_form) Class — ServiceNow Developers](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-plans&identifier=servicenow_administrator&module=learning+plan&release=zurich)

question: Which of the following Link Types should be selected when creating a module that opens the Record Producer UI for a user instead of the ServiceNow form UI?
explanation:
A Record Producer is launched using its catalog-item URL, typically with the producer’s `sysparm_id` supplied as a URL argument. ServiceNow modules that navigate to a target URL use the **URL (from Arguments:)** link type.

**Learn more:** [Set up Platform URLs for catalog modules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_SetURLsForCatalogModules.html) · [Example menu items and content links](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-user-interface/content-management-system/c_NavigationMenusAndContentLinks.html)

question: Which of the following features are available in Studio? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow Studio provides a Code Search feature to find text across all application files, and it integrates with external source control (Git), letting you commit and push changes to an external repository. So the two available features are "Search code" (C) and "Push to external source control" (D). "Push to update set" (A) is not a Studio operation, and "Merge branches" (B) is done in the Git provider rather than inside Studio.

**Learn more:** [Source Control in ServiceNow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-advocate-blog/source-control-in-servicenow-studio-complete-walkthrough/ba-p/3356303)

question: Which Module Link type is used to open an Application Properties page?
explanation:
An Application Properties page is a system property category page that groups an application's properties. A module must navigate to that page by providing its destination in the Arguments field, which is the purpose of the **URL (from Arguments)** link type. ServiceNow documents that this link type opens a URL defined in the Arguments field.

**Learn more:** [Application Navigator category — Module link types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html) · [ServiceNow Studio Navigator panel taxonomy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/servicenow-studio-file-navigator-taxonomy.html)

question: What does Application Scoping offer? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: A method to track users involved in developing the application.

options.label: B
options.text: A namespace (prefix and scope name) to prevent cross-application name collisions.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: A means to control how scripts from other scopes can alter tables in a scoped application.

explanation:
Application scoping gives a scoped application a unique namespace identifier, preventing name collisions with artifacts from other applications. It also restricts cross-scope access, allowing the application and table access settings to determine whether scripts from other scopes can access or alter its tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [ServiceNow: Application access settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationAccessSettings.html)

question: When building an application through the Guided Application Creator, what options are available for creating a table? (select 3)

options.label: C
options.text: Create a table from a template

explanation:
Guided Application Creator creates custom tables by creating one from scratch or by extending an existing extensible table; it also supports creating a table by uploading a spreadsheet. Since the spreadsheet option is not supplied, only “Create a table from scratch” and “Extend a table” are valid among the listed choices.

**Learn more:** [Designate data tables in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-designate-data-table.html) · [Create a table in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-create-table-from-scratch.html?contentId=rgOVQArwcoC4abbhmapHGw)

question: Which of the following statements is true about Application Scope?

Scoped applications use unique namespace identifiers for their artifacts, preventing naming conflicts with applications supplied by third-party ServiceNow developers. The customer prefix within the namespace is system-generated, while scope protections limit cross-scope access and modification.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [ServiceNow Namespace identifier](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_NamespaceIdentifier.html)

question: Which scenario is an example of when an application could use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

options.label: A
options.text: The application needs to run a client-side script at the same time every day.

options.label: B
options.text: The application needs to query the database every day to look for unassigned records.

options.label: C
options.text: To display a custom welcome message when a user logs in.

options.label: D
options.text: To validate form input fields before a record is submitted.

explanation:
A Scheduled Script Execution is used to run a server-side script on a defined schedule. Querying the database each day to identify unassigned records is a recurring background task, so it is an appropriate use of a scheduled job. ServiceNow documents scheduled jobs as automated work performed at a specific time or recurring schedule.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Scheduled jobs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/c_ScheduledJobs.html) · [ServiceNow: Run a script of your choosing](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/t_ScheduleAScriptExecution.html)

question: Which of the following statements is true about GlideUser (`g_user`) methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Can be used in Client Scripts and UI Policies only

options.label: B
options.text: Can be used in Business Rules only

options.label: C
options.text: Can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions

options.label: D
options.text: Can be used in Business Rules, and Scripts Includes

explanation:
GlideUser (`g_user`) is a client-side API for accessing information about the current user and their roles. It can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions that run on the client, but not in Business Rules or server-side UI Actions.

**Learn more:** [GlideUser - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideUserAPI.html)

question: Identify the ways an application can respond to an event generated by the `gs.eventQueue()` method. (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow processes queued events through handlers such as Script Actions and notifications. A Script Action can execute server-side logic for the event, and an Email Notification can send email when the event fires.

**Learn more:** [System Events](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/events.html) · [Create event](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/t_CreateYourOwnEvent.html)

question: What is the ServiceNow Store?

options.label: B
options.text: Alternate name for the ServiceNow Developer Share site

options.label: C
options.text: The source for ServiceNow Community created developer content

options.label: D
options.text: Marketplace for free and paid certified ServiceNow applications and integrations

explanation:
The ServiceNow Store is a marketplace for free and paid certified applications and integrations that extend the ServiceNow platform. Its listings are reviewed or certified to meet ServiceNow standards for stability, performance, and security.

**Learn more:** [Exploring the ServiceNow Store](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/exploring-servicenow-store.html) · [ServiceNow Store third-party application integration guide](https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/success/quick-answer/third-party-application-integration-store.pdf)

question: To identify which scripts, reports, and other application artifacts will be included in a published application:

options.label: A
options.text: Enter the name of the Application in the Global search field

options.label: B
options.text: Open the list of Update Sets for the instance

options.label: C
options.text: Examine the Application Files Related List in the application to be published

options.label: D
options.text: Open the artifact records individually to verify the value in the Application field

explanation:
The application record’s **Application Files** related list is the complete inventory of configuration records owned by the application, including artifacts such as business rules, workflows, and script includes. It is therefore the appropriate place to review the artifacts included with the application. [ServiceNow: Application files](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ApplicationFiles.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Application files](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ApplicationFiles.html)

question: In a Business Rule, which of the following returns the `sys_id` of the currently logged-in user?
explanation:
Business Rules execute on the server, where `gs.getUserID()` returns the `sys_id` of the current user. The `g_form` methods are client-side form APIs and are not the appropriate API in a Business Rule.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideSystem API — getUserID()](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

question: When choosing a data type for a field that will appear on a form, which of the following statements is **NOT** correct?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Phone Number data type to automate phone number data validation

options.label: C
options.text: Use the Choice data type to limit options in a field

options.label: D
options.text: Use the Date data type to enter the date and time of day
