question: Which client-side scripts are applicable to Record Producers? (select 2)
explanation:
Record Producers are Service Catalog items, so their browser-side behavior can be controlled with Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies. ServiceNow documentation identifies both as associated with catalog items and record producers.

**Learn more:** [Catalog Item form](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/catalog-item-form.html) · [Create a Service Catalog client script](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreateACatalogClientScript.html)

question:
A field was deleted from a table, causing it to be removed from several tables.

What type of field was deleted?
explanation:
In ServiceNow, child tables automatically inherit their parent table’s fields. Deleting an inherited field from the parent therefore removes that field from the tables that inherit it. Base system fields cannot be deleted, while reference fields represent relationships and ordinary custom fields are not inherently shared across a table hierarchy.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ServiceNow: Delete a field from a table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-platform-administration/page/administer/reference-pages/task/t_DeleteFields.html)

question: Which of the following is the quickest way to create and configure a Record Producer?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a Catalog Category, open the category, and select the Add New Record Producer button

options.label: B
options.text: Use the Record Producer module then add and configure all variables manually

options.label: C
options.text: Open the table in the Table records and select the Add to Service Catalog Related Link

options.label: D
options.text: Open the table's form, right-click on the form header, and select the Create Record Producer menu item

explanation:
ServiceNow can create a record producer directly from a table record through the **Add to Service Catalog** related link. The process creates the producer for that table and automatically generates variables that correspond to the selected fields, including their types and order.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create record producers from tables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/service-catalog/t_CreatingRecordProducersFromTables.html)

question: Which methods can be used to activate application restricted caller access? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Enable the Cross-Scope Access Override feature in the application settings.

options.label: B
options.text: Request the HR Service Delivery or Security Incident Response applications.

options.label: D
options.text: Activate the Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access plugin.

Application restricted caller access can be enabled by activating the **Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access** plugin or by requesting **HR Service Delivery** or **Security Incident Response**, where it is active by default. Blocking cross-scope access controls requests but does not activate the feature.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Restricted caller access privilege settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/restricted-caller-access-privilege.html) · [ServiceNow: Activate application restricted caller access](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/activate-RCA.html)

question:
The following script fragment is executed in an application:

question: Which platform feature can be used to identify relationships between fields in an Import Set table and fields in an existing ServiceNow table?
explanation: A Transform Map specifies how source fields in an Import Set staging table correspond to target fields in an existing ServiceNow table and can apply transformations during the import.

question:
A developer needs to configure an application module that permits new records to be inserted into a table.

Which configuration option accomplishes this?
explanation:
A ServiceNow module configured with the **New Record** link type displays a form for creating a record in the selected table. The Link type setting controls this module behavior; the Table field only identifies the table used by the module.

**Learn more:** [Application Navigator category](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/automated-test-framework-atf/test-steps-app-navigator-category.html)

question: What does a Module refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: The functionality within an application menu such as opening a page in the content frame or a separate tab or window

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: A way of helping users quickly access information and services by filtering the items in the Application Navigator

options.label: D
options.text: A web-based way of providing software to end-users

explanation:
In ServiceNow, a module is a navigation link within an application menu that opens a page in the content frame or in a separate tab or window. Application menus group related modules; the Application Navigator filter helps users locate them. ოფიციალური ServiceNow documentation defines modules as links that open pages in the content frame or a separate tab or window.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Studio Navigator panel taxonomy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/servicenow-studio-file-navigator-taxonomy.html)

question: What is shown to delegated developers in ServiceNow Studio for packaging changes for deployment?
Which one of the following is **not** an example of a situation in which an application might use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

options.label: A
options.text: The application needs to send weekly email reminders to requestors for all records on a table

options.label: B

question: Which conditions must evaluate to true for a user to pass an Access Control? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: Scripts configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.

options.label: B
options.text: The user must be granted access through a business rule.

options.label: C
options.text: Conditions configured in the Extending table Access Control must evaluate to true.

options.text: The user has one of the roles specified in the Required roles related list.

question: Identify the characteristic(s) of a Record Producer. (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: All records created using this strategy are inserted into the Requested Item [sc_req_item] table.

options.label: B
options.text: Each field prompts the user with a question rather than a field label.

options.label: D

question: Which of the following objects **cannot** be used in a Script Action script?
explanation: Script Actions execute asynchronously in response to an event. They can use the current record and event context, and server-side scripts can create and use `GlideRecord` objects. The `previous` object, which represents the record’s state before an update, is not available in this context.

question: In a privately scoped application, which methods are used to log messages in server-side scripts? (select 2)
explanation:
The scoped GlideSystem API provides `gs.debug()` to write debug-level messages and `gs.error()` to write error-level messages to the system log. [ServiceNow: GlideSystem – Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemScopedAPI.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideSystem – Scoped API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemScopedAPI.html)

question: When configuring an Access Control with no condition or script, which of the following statements is **NOT** true?

options.label: A
options.text: table.*will grant access to every field in a record

options.label: B
options.text: table.None will grant access to every record on the table

options.label: C
options.text: table.field will grant access to a specific field in a record

options.label: D
options.text: table.id will grant access to a specific record on the table

explanation:
ServiceNow evaluates record ACLs at the table and field levels: a table-level ACL applies to the table’s records, `table.*` is a wildcard field ACL, and `table.field` targets a named field. An ACL name does not use `table.id` to select an individual record; access to a specific record must be constrained by record-level conditions or script logic.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html) · [ServiceNow Explore Access Control Lists](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/exploring-access-control-list.html)

question: Which of the following **cannot** be debugged by using the Field Watcher?
explanation:
Field Watcher logs activity on a selected form field, including changes made by Business Rules and Client Scripts, as well as changes to field access rights caused by ACL or dictionary settings. Script Includes are reusable server-side code rather than a Field Watcher event type; debug them with server-side script debugging tools or logs.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Watching fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_FieldWatcher.html) · [ServiceNow: Script Debugger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/script-debugger.html)

question: Which of the following represents the baseline behavior of a table in a privately scoped application?

options.label: A
options.text: The table and its data are not accessible using web services

options.label: B
options.text: Any Business Rule can read, write, delete, and update from the table

options.label: C
options.text: Only artifacts in the table's application can read from the table

options.label: D
options.text: All application scopes can read from the table

explanation:
By default, a table in a privately scoped ServiceNow application can be read by all application scopes. Cross-scope changes to its records require explicit table application-access permissions.

**Learn more:** [Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html) · [Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html)

question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts

options.label: B
options.text: The execution order for a UI Policy's Scripts and Actions is determined at runtime

options.label: C
options.text: A UI Policy's Scripts execute before the UI Policy's Actions

options.label: D
options.text: A UI Policy's Actions and Scripts execute at the same time

explanation:
For a ServiceNow UI Policy, the configured UI Policy Actions are applied before its Execute if true or Execute if false script is run. UI Policy Actions set field attributes such as mandatory, visible, and read-only; the policy script performs its client-side custom logic after those actions have been processed.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow UI policies](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateAUIPolicy.html)

question: A scoped application that contains Flow Designer content dedicated to a particular application is called a(n):
explanation:
A spoke is the scoped application that groups Flow Designer content, such as custom actions and subflows, for a particular application or record type.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Docs — Spokes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/spokes.html?contentId=NATjqw_Hs9Fi_wuKjofx6Q)

question: When you create an application through the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is **NOT** a table-creation option?
explanation:
Guided Application Creator supports creating a custom table from scratch, extending an existing extensible table, or uploading a spreadsheet to create a table. Creating a table from a template is not one of its documented table-creation methods.

**Learn more:** [Designate data tables in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-designate-data-table.html) · [Create a table in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-create-table-from-scratch.html)

question: The Task table is an example of which of the following? (select 2)
explanation:
The ServiceNow Task table is a parent class because Incident, Problem, and Change Request extend it. It is also a base class, providing common fields and functionality to those extending tables.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table extension and classes](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-extension-and-classes.html?contentId=tcFq_LsUEHYP0jZ1YWKwsg) · [ServiceNow: Important Task table fields](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/r_ImportantTaskTableFields.html)

question: What do tables that extend another table do?

options.label: B
options.text: Do not inherit the parent’s fields

explanation:
A child table that extends a parent table inherits the parent table’s fields, while it can also define fields unique to the child table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ServiceNow: Table relationships](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/table-relationships.html)

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a method for logging messages in a server-side script within a privately scoped application?
explanation:
For scoped ServiceNow applications, the GlideSystem logging methods include `gs.debug()`, `gs.warn()`, and `gs.error()`. `gs.log()` belongs to the global GlideSystem API rather than the scoped API.

**Learn more:** [GlideSystem - Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemScopedAPI.html) · [GlideSystem - Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

question: Which of these statements is true about Guided Application Creator?

options.label: A
options.text: The global scope option is turned on by default

options.label: B
options.text: Default access controls are automatically created

options.label: C
options.text: The welcome screen appears every time a new application is created

options.label: D
options.text: A scoped application user role is automatically created

explanation:
During table creation, ServiceNow automatically configures access control for a newly created or selected role, restricting read, create, write, and delete access to users with that role. Global-scope app creation is disabled by default, the welcome screen is shown on the first launch, and application roles are explicitly selected or created.

**Learn more:** [Secure data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/secure-data.html) · [Create an application record in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-create-app-record.html)

question: Which ServiceNow Studio-supported file type customizes system behavior by means of database actions?
explanation:
Business Rules are server-side configuration records in the `sys_script` table. They run when database actions, including query, insert, update, and delete, occur and are used to customize system behavior.

**Learn more:** [Supported code search file types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/sn-studio-file-types.html)

question: What is the ServiceNow Application Repository?

options.label: C
options.text: A collection of files in a Git database

explanation: The ServiceNow App Repository is a repository that stores ServiceNow applications for distribution and installation.

question: What occurs to the List view when a new field is added to an existing table?

options.label: A
options.text: The new field is added at the start of the List

options.label: B
options.text: The new field is added at the end of the List

options.label: C
options.text: The new field is not added to the List view

options.label: D
options.text: A List View is created with the new Field

explanation:
When a new field is added to an existing table, ServiceNow automatically places it on the default form (at the end of the first section) but does NOT automatically add it to the List view. List layouts are controlled separately and must be updated manually via Configure > List Layout to surface the new column. Therefore the new field is not added to the List view, making C correct; the existing answer B (added at the end of the list) confuses form behavior with list behavior.

**Learn more:** [Adding Fields to a Table](https://developer.servicenow.com/dev.do#!/learn/learning-plans/xanadu/new_to_servicenow/app_store_learnv2_buildneedit_xanadu_adding_fields_to_a_table)

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a purpose of application scoping?

options.label: A
options.text: Provide a relationship between application artifacts

options.label: B
options.text: Provide a way of tracking the user who developed an application

options.label: C
options.text: Provide a namespace (prefix and scope name) to prevent cross application name collisions

options.label: D
options.text: Provide controls for how scripts from another scope can alter tables in a scoped application

explanation: Application scoping supplies a namespace to avoid naming collisions, relates application artifacts within a scope, and enforces cross-scope controls over access to scoped resources. Tracking the user who developed an application is not a function of application scoping.

question: When troubleshooting Email Notifications, what must be verified on a user record? (select 2)

options.label: B
options.text: The Email field must have a valid value.

options.label: C
options.text: The user must not be locked out.

options.label: D
options.text: The First name and Last name fields must have values.

explanation:
Email-notification recipients must have an active user profile and a valid email address; otherwise, the notification is not received. Locked-out status, first and last names, and delegation are not general prerequisites for outbound email delivery.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html?contentId=650y12ua2_GdSIzlfDV50g)

question: Where can GlideUser (`g.user`) methods be used within ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: Client Scripts and UI Policies only

options.label: C
options.text: Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions

explanation:
The GlideUser client API exposes current-user information through the client-side `g_user` object. It is used in Client Scripts and UI Policies and is also available in UI Actions that run in the browser; it cannot be used in server-side Business Rules or Script Includes.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideUser - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideUserAPI.html)

question: How can an application respond to an event initiated by the `gs.eventQueue()` method? (select 2)
explanation:
ServiceNow event processing can invoke a Script Action or send a notification when a queued event is handled. `gs.eventQueue()` creates the event record, and the event handler routes it to configured actions such as script actions and notifications.

**Learn more:** [System Events](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/events.html) · [Event registry](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/system-events/c_EventRegistry.html)

question: Which actions can a Business Rule perform without using scripting?

options.label: A
options.text: Set field values and write to the system log

options.label: B
options.text: Set field values and generate an event

options.label: C
options.text: Set field values and add message

options.label: D
options.text: Set field values and query the database

explanation:
Business Rules provide built-in Actions for setting field values and displaying a message to the user. System-log writes, event generation, and database queries require scripting.

**Learn more:** [Classic Business rules](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)

question: What happens when an existing table is extended in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: The parent table's Access Controls are ignored when determining access to the new table's records and fields.

options.label: B
options.text: The new table does not inherit any of the fields from the parent table.

options.label: C
options.text: You must script and configure all required behaviors.

options.label: D
options.text: The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table.

explanation:
A child table in ServiceNow inherits the fields and functionality of its parent table, while it can also add child-specific fields and configuration. This inheritance supports consistent behavior across related record types.

**Learn more:** [Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html)

question: Which business requirements and process(es) should be recorded as part of the application development plan? (select 4)
explanation: An application development plan should define the business problem to solve, the process steps the application must support, the users and stakeholders affected, and the project schedule for delivery. These elements establish the business need, operational workflow, participants, and planning timeline.

question: Which Flow Variable data types are supported for storing record data? (select 3)
explanation:
Flow variables that store record data must use a type matching the source record field. Date, Integer, and String are supported record-data types. Arrays are complex-data containers, while a choice value is stored through its underlying field type rather than as a generic Choice Flow Variable type.

**Learn more:** [Workflow Studio input and output data variables](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/build-workflows/workflow-studio/action-inputs-outputs.html) · [Integer data type](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/integer-data.html)

question: Which method retrieves Application Property values in a script?
explanation:
The GlideSystem API method `gs.getProperty()` returns the value of a Glide property by its key. [ServiceNow GlideSystem API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideSystem API](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideSystemAPI.html)

question: Which factors are reasons that an application might be developed on the ServiceNow platform? (select 3)

options.label: A
options.text: It needs workflow to manage processes.

options.label: C
options.text: It uses forms extensively to interact with data.

explanation:
The ServiceNow platform supports applications that automate business processes through workflows, present and analyze record data through reporting and analytics, and use forms to let users interact with data. These are core application-platform capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Building apps in ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/overview-building-apps-in-servicenow.html) · [Overview of reporting and analytics for developers](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/reporting-and-dashboards.html)

question: Which choices are approaches for debugging client-side scripts? (select 2)
explanation:
`jslog()` records client-side diagnostic output in the JavaScript Log. `g_form.addInfoMessage()` is a client-side GlideForm method that displays a message on the form, making it useful for inspecting script behavior. The `gs` APIs are server-side APIs and are not available to client-side scripts.

**Learn more:** [Writing to the debug log](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/scripts/c_WritingToTheDebugLog.html?contentId=in00Mtq8nyOP7KmekAuzAQ) · [GlideForm (g_form) - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideFormAPI.html)

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Application Picker?

options.label: A
options.text: All custom application scope and the Global scope appear in the Application Picker

options.label: B
options.text: All applications in ServiceNow, including baseline applications like Incident, appear in the Application Picker

options.label: C
options.text: Only custom applications appear in the Application Picker

options.label: D
options.text: Only downloaded applications appear in the Application Picker

explanation:
The Application Picker lets developers select the application scope in which changes apply. It lists the Global scope and custom application scopes accessible to the user, rather than every baseline application as an individual entry. ServiceNow documents that the picker opens a list of application scopes available to the user.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Application picker](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationPicker.html) · [ServiceNow Global scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_GlobalScope.html)

question: When configuring a module, what does the **Override application menu roles** configuration option do?

options.label: A
options.text: Users with the module role but without access to the application menu access the module

options.label: B
options.text: Self-Service users can access the module even though they do not have roles

options.label: C
options.text: Admin is given access to the module even if Access Controls would ordinarily prevent access

options.label: D
options.text: Users with access to the application menu can see the module even if they don't have the module role

explanation:
When selected, module roles override application-menu roles. A user who meets the module’s role requirement can access the module even when the containing application menu’s roles would not ordinarily allow access.

**Learn more:** [Create a List Module](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/cRO8ZxW3MhqqdUt8Tydjtg/8BjlvbFlpDZhe3Z8ZzoLyw)

question: Which client-side scoped API class can serve as a replacement for GlideRecord?
explanation:
GlideAjax lets a client script invoke server-side code in a client-callable Script Include to retrieve or process record data. ServiceNow specifies GlideAjax as the alternative to client-side GlideRecord in scoped applications.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideRecord - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/api-reference/c_GlideRecordClientSideAPI.html) · [ServiceNow GlideAjax - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideAjaxAPI.html)

question: Which of the following statements does **not** apply when you extend an existing table?

options.label: A
options.text: The parent table's Access Controls are evaluated when determining access to the new table's records and fields

options.label: B
options.text: The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table

options.label: C
options.text: The new table inherits all of the fields from the parent table

options.label: D
options.text: You must script and configure all required behaviors

explanation:
A child table inherits the parent table’s fields and functionality, and parent-table ACLs apply to tables that extend that parent. Extending a table therefore does not require scripting and configuring all required behavior again.

**Learn more:** [Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: Why should Applications be created in ServiceNow?
explanation: Creating ServiceNow applications can replace outdated or inadequate custom business applications and processes, broaden service delivery and management to enterprise departments, and extend the value of the ServiceNow platform. Application creation does not provide users with unrestricted access to all tables, records, and fields, because access is governed by platform security controls.

question: Which methods can be used to designate data tables in Guided Application Creator (GAC)? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new table on the platform

options.label: E
options.text: Use an existing table on the platform

options.label: F
options.text: Upload an existing word processing document

explanation:
Guided Application Creator supports selecting an existing platform table, creating a new custom table, or uploading a spreadsheet to generate a custom table. These are the available table-designation methods; document uploads and a freeform database are not supported methods.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Designate data tables in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-designate-data-table.html) · [ServiceNow: Upload a spreadsheet in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-upload-spreadsheet.html)

question: What is the purpose of the **coalesce** field during data import?

options.label: A
options.text: If a match is not found, the existing record is updated

options.label: B
options.text: To determine if a record matches an existing record or is a new record

options.label: C
options.text: To identify and merge duplicate records

options.label: D
options.text: When a match is found, a new record is inserted

explanation:
A coalesce field acts as a matching key during an import transform. ServiceNow checks whether the imported value matches an existing target-table record; a match updates that record, while no match creates a new record.

**Learn more:** [Updating records using coalesce](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/system-import-sets/c_ImportSetCoalesce.html)

question: How does ServiceNow associate an inbound email with an existing record?
explanation: ServiceNow uses an email watermark to correlate replies with the existing record that generated the outbound message.

question:
You are developing the MyApp application, which contains a table named Table A. When MyApp is installed on an instance, you want the records in Table A to be installed as part of the application.

Table A's records will be installed when:

options.label: A
options.text: Table A is active and extends the Task table

options.label: B
options.text: Table A's records are added to the application record using the Create Application Files context menu item

options.label: C
options.text: Table A has an automatic number counter for new records

options.label: D
options.text: Table A is not included in the System Clone > Exclude Tables list

explanation:
Selected records from an application data table are included with an application by using **Create Application Files**, which adds them to the application's application files. The Load When setting can include those data records during a new installation.

**Learn more:** [Create application files to include sample data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/t_IncludeApplicationData.html)

question: When you create new application files in a scoped application, for which of the following is cross-scope access enabled by default?
explanation:
A table in a scoped application is created with its cross-scope accessibility set to allow access from all application scopes by default. Other scopes can therefore access it subject to the table’s configured application-access and operation permissions.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Application Development answer guide](https://www.servicenow.com/community/s/cgfwn76974/attachments/cgfwn76974/training-certifications-kb/8346/3/ADF_AnswerGuide_U010.pdf) · [Define cross-scope access to an application resource](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/application-development/set-RCA-level.html)

question: Which of the following may serve as an external data source for a ServiceNow application?

options.label: B
options.text: Data provided by a public web service using SOAP or REST

explanation:
ServiceNow Integration Hub imports can use Excel files, CSV files, or a Data Stream action. A Data Stream action can send REST or SOAP requests to an API and return data, so Excel, CSV, and public SOAP/REST web services can all be external data sources.

**Learn more:** [Integration Hub - Import](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/integration-hub/integrationhub-imports.html)

question: Which of the following database operations can be controlled with Application Access? (select 2)
explanation:
A table's Application Access settings govern which database operations other application scopes may perform on the table. For this CAD item the two controlled operations are Create (C) and Update (B). The existing key of three letters (Update, Create, Delete) violates the "choose two" constraint; ServiceNow community consensus for this exact question is Create and Update. Query/read is broadly accessible by default and is not part of the keyed answer.

**Learn more:** [Securing an application using Cross Scope Access & Application Access](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-blog/securing-an-application-using-cross-scope-access-application/ba-p/2288801)

question: Application developers configure ServiceNow with industry-standard JavaScript to…

options.label: A
options.text: Enable the right-click to edit the context menus on applications in the navigator

options.label: C
options.text: Customize the organization's company logo and banner text

options.label: D
options.text: Configure the outgoing email display name

explanation: Industry-standard JavaScript is used in ServiceNow development to extend platform capabilities and implement additional application functionality.

question: Which of the following is **NOT** true about Modules?

options.label: B
options.text: Access to Modules is controlled with roles

options.label: C
options.text: Every Module must be part of an Application Menu

options.label: D
options.text: Every Module must be associated with a table

explanation:
ServiceNow modules can link to different destination types, including content pages, URLs, and table-based lists or forms. Only table-oriented module types require a table, so a module is not universally required to be associated with one. Roles can restrict access to modules, and modules are organized under application menus.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Studio Classic Navigator panel taxonomy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/servicenow-studio-file-navigator-taxonomy.html) · [Grant role access](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/t_GrantARoleAccessToAppsAndModules.html)

question: How does the value in the **Weight** field affect the sending of multiple notifications for the same record and recipients?

options.label: A
options.text: Notifications with the highest weight value are always skipped.

options.label: B
options.text: Notifications with the lowest weight value are sent.

options.label: C
options.text: Notifications with a weight value of zero are skipped.

options.label: D
options.text: Notifications with the highest weight value are sent.

explanation:
For duplicate notifications with the same target record and recipients, ServiceNow uses a nonzero Weight value as priority and sends the notification with the highest weight. A Weight of 0 is sent independently, provided its conditions are met.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: What is the Event Registry?

options.label: A
options.text: A Workflow which is launched every time an Event is generated; used to debug Events

options.label: B
options.text: The Event Log which lists all Events that have been generated

options.label: C
options.text: The method used in server side scripts to generate Events and pass parameters

options.label: D
options.text: A table containing a record for every Event known to the ServiceNow system which allows ServiceNow to react when Events are generated

explanation: The Event Registry is a ServiceNow table that contains a record for each event known to the instance, enabling ServiceNow to respond when those events are generated.

question: When a new application table is created, what is the default module name?

options.label: A
options.text: X_' prefixed to the application name

options.label: B
options.text: Plural form of the application name

options.label: C
options.text: Same name as the application name

explanation: A newly created ServiceNow application table receives a navigation module whose default name uses the plural form of the application name. Prefixes such as `x_` and `u_` are table-name conventions, not the default module label.

question: What is one advantage of creating an Application Properties page for every application?

options.label: A
options.text: Developers or admins can adjust behavior without altering artifacts

options.label: B
options.text: Acts as a central larding page for the application

options.label: C
options.text: Developers can override inherited application properties

options.label: D
options.text: Users can modify the appearance of the application

explanation:
An Application Properties page externalizes configurable behavior into application-level properties, allowing developers or administrators to adjust settings without modifying the underlying application artifacts.

**Learn more:** [Application properties | Pega Academy](https://academy.pega.com/topic/application-properties/v1)

question: Which plugin enables the Guided Application Creator?
explanation:
Guided Application Creator is enabled through the Guided Application Creator plugin, whose identifier is `com.glide.sn-guided-app-creator`.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/application-development/guided-application-creator/guided-app-creator.html)

question: What occurs when an existing table is extended? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: All required behavior must be newly scripted and configured from the new table.

options.label: B
options.text: Specific fields from the parent table can be selected to be inherited.

options.label: C
options.text: Parent table Access Controls are also evaluated while determining access for the new table.

options.label: D
options.text: The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table.

options.label: E
options.text: The new table inherits all the fields from the parent table.

options.label: F
options.text: Dictionary entries for the new table also include records for fields from the parent table.

explanation: When a table extends another table in the ServiceNow class hierarchy, the extended table automatically inherits every field already defined on the parent table without requiring any additional configuration, and it also inherits the functionality already built on the parent, such as business rules, client scripts, and UI policies, so that behavior does not need to be recreated on the new table. This automatic inheritance of both fields and functionality is the defining characteristic of extending a table in ServiceNow's table hierarchy.

question: What is one limitation of using record producers in ServiceNow?

options.label: A
options.text: Record producers cannot redirect users after record creation

options.label: B
options.text: Record producers cannot he used for tables in the same scope

options.label: C
options.text: Record producers should not be used to create requested item records

options.label: D
options.text: Record producers must always call the update method on the current record

explanation: Record producers are intended to create records in a target table through a catalog-style interface, not to create requested item records. Requested items must be created through the Service Catalog request process so that the related request, fulfillment, and catalog-item data is established correctly.

question: Which ServiceNow table stores the details of customizations included in an update set?
explanation:
The Customer Update table (`sys_update_xml`) contains the records for individual customized objects associated with an update set. The Update Set table (`sys_update_set`) stores the update set itself.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: System update sets](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/yokohama-application-development/page/build/system-update-sets/concept/system-update-sets.html)

question: What are web services?

options.label: A
options.text: Methods used to create and maintain UI Pages

options.label: B
options.text: Methods used to allow applications to connect to other software applications over a network

options.label: C
options.text: Methods used to discover a wide variety of systems and applications

options.label: D
options.text: They provide a customer-facing view of available service and product offerings provided by departments within the organization

explanation: Web services provide methods that let applications communicate and connect with other software applications across a network.

question: Which statement is true about deleting fields from a table?

options.label: A
options.text: Table records are deleted when a field is deleted

options.label: B
options.text: User-defined non-inherited fields can be deleted

options.label: C
options.text: Any field on a table can be deleted

explanation: User-defined fields that are defined directly on a table, rather than inherited from a parent table, can be deleted. Deleting a field does not delete the table's records, and inherited fields cannot be deleted from the child table.

question: What do client-side scripts manage?
explanation: Client-side scripts execute in the user’s browser and manage interactive interface elements such as forms and form fields.

question: Flow Designer supports variable data types for storing record data and complex data. Which of the following variable data types are supported? (select 3)
explanation:
Flow Designer supports Choice and Integer data variables, and it supports an array of Boolean values, documented as `Array.Boolean`. The supported array parent types do not include `Array.Reference`; `Label` and `Freedom` are not Flow Designer variable data types.

**Learn more:** [Complex data](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/en-US/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/concept/complex-data.html) · [Array.Boolean data type](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/washingtondc/build-workflows/array-boolean-data.html?contentId=emGPQdSpSo~Slwl9VBqO9A)

question: When configuring a REST Message, what is the Endpoint?

options.label: B
options.text: The command to the REST script to stop execution

options.label: C
options.text: Tne URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified

options.label: D
options.text: The provider response indicates there is no data to send back

explanation:
For a ServiceNow REST message, the endpoint is the URL/URI identifying the data resource to be retrieved, updated, or deleted. It identifies the data that the REST operation accesses, queries, or modifies.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow REST message elements](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/web-services/r_RESTMessageElements.html)

question: Which of the following is a benefit of creating an Application Properties page for every application you develop?

options.label: A
options.text: Application Properties allow a developer to override the application properties inherited from ServiceNow

options.label: B
options.text: An Application Properties page is a good landing page for an application

options.label: C
options.text: Application Properties allow a developer or admin to make changes to an application's behavior without modifying application artifacts

options.label: D
options.text: Application users know to go to the Application Properties page to change the appearance of an application

explanation:
Application properties provide configurable parameters that can change an application's behavior without altering its application artifacts. This allows authorized developers or administrators to adjust behavior through configuration rather than modifying the underlying application implementation.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow AI Platform glossary — application properties](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/glossary/now-platform-glossary.html)

question:
Assume that a table named `table` exists and includes three fields: `field1`, `field2`, and `field3`. Review the access control list for `table`:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1784203684742-idgd2xqx.png)

Which field or fields can a user assigned the `itil` role read?
explanation:
A user with the `itil` role passes the table-level `table.None` read ACL. For `field3`, the more-specific `table.field3` ACL permits `itil`, and a successful specific field ACL stops further field-level evaluation. `field1` and `field2` fall through to `table.*`, which requires the `admin` role. ServiceNow evaluates field ACLs from specific fields to wildcard fields after table access is granted.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow ACL types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/acl-rule-types.html)

question: Why are application files significant? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: They store user credentials for the application.

options.label: B
options.text: They define the app logic and behavior.

options.label: C
options.text: They restrict access to the application.

explanation: Application files are significant because they are the actual building blocks that implement an application's logic and behavior (scripts, UI elements, workflows, and configuration records that make the app function), and because each file can be assigned an access/protection level that restricts who can view, edit, or customize it, which is how ServiceNow enforces intellectual-property protection and controlled customization for scoped applications; storing user credentials and monitoring performance metrics are not functions performed by application files themselves.

question: Under what circumstance can the value "Protected" be used in a Protected Policy for a Script Include?

options.label: A
options.text: A user with the admin role enables the Policy option

options.label: B
options.text: The glide.app.apply_protection system property is set to "True"

options.label: C
options.text: The application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store

options.label: D
options.text: A user with the protected_edit role edits the Script Include

explanation:
A Script Include with a **Protected** protection policy is encrypted on instances where its application is installed from the ServiceNow Store. Protection policies do not apply on the instance where the application is developed.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers — Script Include protection policy](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-module&identifier=SSS_About_zurich%2Cservicenow_administrator&module=learning+plan&release=zurich)

question: Which of the following database operations cannot be controlled through Application Access?
explanation:
Application Access controls table-record permissions through read, create, update, and delete settings. It has no separate Query operation setting; querying records is covered by read access. [ServiceNow: Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question: When configuring an Email Notification’s content, which syntax should you use to reference properties of the event that triggered the notification?
explanation:
ServiceNow exposes the triggering event as the `event` object in event-based email notifications. Notification variable substitution references an event property with `${event.<property name>}`; `current` instead represents the notification’s associated record.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html) · [Advanced conditions for email notifications](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_OptSpecifyingAdvancedCond.html)

question: When creating application tables, an application user role is automatically added to the table record. Which additional role does an application typically have?
explanation:
ServiceNow applications commonly use both an application user role and an application-specific admin role. The admin role authorizes administration of the application and assignment of its application-specific roles.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow — Create an application in ServiceNow Studio](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-studio-classic/create-an-application-in-servicenow-studio.html) · [ServiceNow — Application administration](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/application-administration.html)

question: Which server-side object supplies methods for working with dates while writing a script in a privately scoped application?
explanation:
GlideDateTime is the server-side API object for date-time operations, including instantiation, date-time calculations, formatting, and conversion between date-time formats. In scoped applications, its scoped API provides the applicable date and time methods.

**Learn more:** [GlideDateTime - Scoped](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideDateTimeScoped.html)

question: Which of the following is **not** a trigger type in Flow Designer?
explanation: Flow Designer uses Record, Schedule, and Application triggers to start flows. Sending an outbound email is performed as an action within a flow, not as a trigger type.

question: In which scenario would a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) be implemented?

options.label: A
options.text: The application executes a client-side script daily at the same time.

options.label: B
options.text: The application displays a custom welcome message when a user logs in.

options.label: C
options.text: The application queries the database daily to check unassigned records.

options.label: D
options.text: The application validates form input fields before a record is submitted.

explanation:
A Scheduled Script Execution is used to run server-side work automatically at a specified time or recurring interval, such as a daily query that identifies unassigned records. ServiceNow documents daily execution as a scheduled-job interval and allows a script to run at the scheduled date and time.

**Learn more:** [Run a script of your choosing](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/time-configuration/t_ScheduleAScriptExecution.html)

question: How can an application be linked to a repository that is behind a firewall?

options.label: B
options.text: Link an application to source control through a MID Server.

options.label: C
options.text: Link an application to source control through an access token.

options.label: D
options.text: Link an application to source control with multi-factor authentication.

explanation:
A ServiceNow MID Server provides the connection path to a source-control repository behind a firewall. ServiceNow documents that configuring or accessing an application through a MID Server enables access to Git repositories located behind a firewall.

**Learn more:** [Configure a MID Server to use source control](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/servicenow-ide-family-release/configure-mid-server-source-control.html)

question: Which source-control operation can be performed from both Studio and the Git Repository?
explanation:
Creating a branch is supported in both UiPath Studio’s Git branch-management workflow and a Git repository. Studio documentation describes adding branches from the Manage Branches window.

**Learn more:** [UiPath Studio — Creating and Managing Branches](https://docs.uipath.com/studio/standalone/latest/user-guide/creating-and-managing-branches)

question:
Which of the following statements about Form Designer are true?

- a) To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the **Fields** tab to the intended location on the form.
- b) To create a new field on a form's table, drag the relevant data type from the **Field Types** tab onto the form, then configure the new field.
- c) To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, then select the Delete (X) button.
- d) To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the **Field Types** tab to the intended location on the form.
explanation:
In Form Designer, existing fields are added by dragging them from the **Fields** tab, new table fields are created by dragging a data type from the **Field Types** tab onto the form and configuring it, and a field is removed from the layout with its hover Remove (X) button. A section, however, is not dragged from the Field Types tab; it is added by selecting an existing section and using the (+) button beside the section label. Statements a, b and c are therefore true and d is not.

**Learn more:** [Using the form designer](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/c_FormDesign.html)

question: When troubleshooting and debugging notifications, where do you navigate to determine whether an email was sent in response to an event?
explanation:
ServiceNow stores each notification email in an Email [sys_email] record. The System Logs > Emails module displays those records, including sent status and the originating event and notification.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: System email log](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/fr-FR/platform-security/r_EmailLogs.html?contentId=sbHCPNKkh0uAwzVXxHNDZg)

question:
What are some benefits of extending an existing table, such as the Task table, when you create a new application?

- a) You can reuse existing fields by simply changing their label.
- b) Use existing fields without making modifications.
- c) Existing logic from the parent table is automatically applied to the new table.
- d) All records from the parent table are copied to the new table.
explanation:
A child table inherits the parent table’s fields and functionality. Inherited fields can be used unchanged, and a child table can override an inherited field’s label when a similar existing field serves the needed purpose. Extending a table does not copy every parent-table record into the child table.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Tables and data models](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/tables-and-data-models.html) · [ServiceNow: Build the data model](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/build-data-model.html)

question: What can a developer accomplish by using REST API Explorer? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: Practice using REST to interact with public data providers

options.label: B
options.text: Convert REST Message functions to REST methods

options.label: C
options.text: Find resources on the web for learning about REST

options.label: D
options.text: Create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow

explanation:
REST API Explorer lets developers construct and execute REST requests against ServiceNow API endpoints, inspect the responses, and obtain generated code samples for those requests in multiple programming languages.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow REST APIs documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/rest-api-explorer/c_RESTAPI.html)

question: Which objects are included in the client-side scripting API? (select 2)
explanation: The client-side ServiceNow scripting API includes g_form for interacting with form data and controls, and g_user for accessing details about the logged-in user. The other listed objects are server-side APIs or execution-context variables.

question: For an Email Notification, which of the following statements about the **Weight** field is NOT true?

options.label: A
options.text: Only Notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipients are sent

options.label: B
options.text: A Weight value of zero means that no email should be sent

options.label: C
options.text: The Weight value defaults to zero

options.label: D
options.text: A Weight value of zero means the Notification is always sent when the Notification's When to send criteria is met

explanation:
A Weight value of 0 is the default and causes the notification to be sent when its sending criteria are met. Nonzero weights prioritize duplicate notifications for the same target record and recipients; the highest weight is sent. Thus, zero does not mean that no email is sent.

**Learn more:** [Create an email notification](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_CreateANotification.html)

question: When creating a Client Script intended to display feedback tied to a particular field, which method should be used?
explanation:
The GlideForm client-side API method g_form.showFieldMsg(fieldName, message, type, scrollForm) is specifically designed to render a message directly associated with a given field on the form, unlike showInfoMessage() or addInfoMessage(), which display general messages at the top of the entire form rather than next to a specific field. There is no addFieldMsg() method in the GlideForm API, making showFieldMsg() the correct and only valid choice for field-level feedback in Client Scripts.

**Learn more:** [Behavior of g_form.showFieldMsg() - ServiceNow Community](https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-forum/behavior-of-g-form-showfieldmsg/m-p/2725384) · [Configuring 'showErrorBox' and 'showFieldMsg' with hideFieldMsg for a better UI experience](https://noderegister.service-now.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB0784211)

question:
The **Exportitem** table extends the **Item** table by adding the **ItemCountry** column. The **Item** table contains the **ItemName** and **ItemQty** columns.

Which fields are available in the **ExportItem** table?
explanation: A table extension retains the fields of its base table and adds its own extension fields. ExportItem therefore has ItemName and ItemQty from Item, along with ItemCountry.

question: When configuring a REST Message, what is the Endpoint?

options.label: A
options.text: The commands to the REST script to stop execution

options.label: B
options.text: The URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified

options.label: C
options.text: Information about the format of the returned data

options.label: D
options.text: The response from the provider indicating there is no data to send back

explanation: A REST endpoint is the URI that identifies the data or resource to access, query, or modify.

question: Which events can initiate a Flow in Workflow Studio Flow Designer? (select 3)

options.label: F
options.text: Logging in as a specific user

explanation:
Flow Designer (Workflow Studio) offers distinct trigger types, three of which appear here: a Record trigger fired when a record is created or updated (B), a REST/inbound API trigger that lets an external system initiate the flow via an API call (D), and an SLA Task trigger fired when a task SLA reaches a breach threshold (E). The other options are not triggers: Flow Designer triggers on INBOUND email, not outbound (A); there is no trigger for elevating to security_admin (C); and there is no "log in as a specific user" trigger (F). Both supplied answers were wrong because they included a non-trigger (outbound email in one, login in the other).

**Learn more:** [Flow trigger types](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/zurich-build-workflows/page/administer/flow-designer/reference/flow-triggers.html) · [REST API trigger](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/integrate-applications/integration-hub/rest-trigger.html)

question: When a ServiceNow instance requests data from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service:
explanation: A consumer is the system that sends requests to and uses a web service. A provider is the system that exposes the web service.

question: What do server-side scripts manage?
explanation: Server-side scripts execute on the server to implement backend application logic and commonly read from, write to, and otherwise manage database-backed operations.

question: Access Control debug information indicates whether every Access Control element allowed or denied access. The elements are shown in the debug information in their evaluation order. In what order are an Access Control's elements evaluated?
explanation:
Within a ServiceNow Access Control, role requirements are evaluated before conditions, and conditions are evaluated before scripts. ServiceNow also evaluates security attributes after roles and before conditions when they are present.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Access Analyzer Debug logs](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/access-control/access-analyzer-logs.html)

question: A basic strategy exists for creating a Utils Script Include. Identify the step that does not belong.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a prototype object from the new class

explanation: A Utils Script Include holds reusable, generally table-independent functions. Creating the class, defining its prototype object, and scripting its functions are part of the standard structure; identifying a table is not required.

question: Which method call returns `true` only when the currently logged-in user has the `catalog_admin` role, and not in any other case?
explanation:
`g_user.hasRoleExactly('catalog_admin')` checks whether the current user has that specific role. Unlike `hasRole()`, it does not return `true` merely because the user has the `admin` role.

**Learn more:** [GlideUser - Client](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/c_GlideUserAPI.html)

question: Why might you build a custom app? (select 2)

options.label: A
options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab

options.label: C
options.text: To fulfill a specific use case on internal processes

options.label: D
options.text: To create a custom integration for a 3rd party system

explanation: Custom applications support specific internal business-process use cases and can provide tailored integrations with third-party systems. They do not replace ServiceNow base tables or eliminate the need for source control.

question: When you create an application with the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is a user-experience option?
explanation:
Mobile is a Guided Application Creator user experience, allowing users to access an application through the ServiceNow Agent mobile app. The other listed items are not available user-experience selections in Guided Application Creator.

**Learn more:** [Select user experiences in Guided Application Creator](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/yokohama/application-development/guided-application-creator/gac-select-ux.html)

question: Which three methods can be used to create a ServiceNow table? (select 3)

options.label: B
options.text: Upload and turn a spreadsheet into a custom table

options.label: D
options.text: Use the Now Experience Table Creator

explanation:
ServiceNow supports creating a table by uploading a spreadsheet to supply fields, extending an existing ServiceNow table and adding fields, or creating a table from scratch as a custom table. These are the three documented table-creation strategies in Guided App Creator.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow Developers — Guided App Creator: Data Pane](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=course-module&identifier=app_store_learnv2_buildmyfirstapp_zurich_guided_app_creator_and_servicenow_studio%2CSTB_About_zurich&module=course&release=zurich)

question: When the **Create module** field is selected while creating a table, what is the default behavior of the newly created module?

options.label: A
options.text: Open an empty form so new records can be created

options.label: B
options.text: Open a link to a wiki article with instructions on how to customize the behavior of the new module

options.label: C
options.text: Display an empty homepage for the application

options.label: D
options.text: Display a list of all records from the table

explanation:
Selecting **Create module** when creating a ServiceNow table creates a list module in the application menu. That module opens the list view containing the table’s records.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Create a table](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/table-administration-and-data-management/t_CreateATable.html?contentId=8EfyhC9ilIfGGhbCb3bm0Q)

question:
Here is the Business Rule script template:

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783795636303-7b1ldzus.png)

This kind of JavaScript function is called:
explanation:
An immediately invoked function expression is defined and called at once. The trailing `(current, previous)` invokes the wrapped function expression immediately, making it a self-invoking function.

**Learn more:** [MDN JavaScript Functions Guide — Immediately Invoked Function Expressions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Functions)

question: What does the **Read-only** protection policy for Script Includes permit in a custom application?

options.label: A
options.text: Application developers can customize the Script Include.

options.label: B
options.text: Only administrators can delete the Script Include.

options.label: C
options.text: Application developers can view the script logic but not change it.

options.label: D
options.text: Only administrators can edit the Script Include.

explanation:
The Read-only protection policy lets other application developers view the Script Include’s logic but prevents them from modifying it.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Script protection policy](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/building-applications/c_ScriptProtectionPolicy.html)

question: Which syntax is used in a Record Producer script to access values from Record Producer form fields?
explanation: Record Producer form values are exposed through the `producer` object and referenced by their variable name, using `producer.<variable_name>`. The `current` object refers to the target record being created, not the submitted producer variables.

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a method for installing an application on a ServiceNow instance?

options.label: A
options.text: Install an application from the Application Repository

options.label: B
options.text: Select the Copy button on the application record

options.label: C
options.text: Download and install an application from the ServiceNow Share web site

options.label: D
options.text: Download and install a third-party application from the ServiceNow Store

explanation:
ServiceNow supports installing entitled applications from the Application Repository and applications procured through the ServiceNow Store. Selecting **Copy** on an application record only creates a copy of that record; it does not install an application on an instance.

**Learn more:** [Install an application from the application repository](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/application-repository-self-hosted/install-app-from-repo.html?contentId=WUw8_bdS3tolY9Ajn7Du4Q) · [Install a ServiceNow Store application](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/t_InstallApplications.html)

question: A graphical representation of the relationships between tables is called a <blank>.
explanation: A schema map displays database tables visually and shows the relationships that connect them.

question:
An application named My App contains a table named MyAppTable with the following Application Access configuration:

- Accessible from: All application scopes
- Can read: Selected
- Can delete: Not selected
- Allow configuration: Selected

Which statement is true for this configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: An application developer working in another privately scoped application can write a Business Rule for the MyAppTable table which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table

options.label: B
options.text: An application developer working in the My App scope can write a Business Rule for the MyAppTable table which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table

options.label: C
options.text: Any Application developer can write a Business Rule which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable

options.label: D
options.text: No Business Rule can be written which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table

explanation:
An application can access and modify tables within its own scope. The unselected Can delete setting specifically prevents script objects in other application scopes from deleting records from the table; it does not prevent a Business Rule in the table-owning My App scope from doing so. Allow configuration permits cross-scope creation of supported configuration records, but it does not grant cross-scope delete permission.

**Learn more:** [Application scope](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/c_ApplicationScope.html) · [Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question:
An app developer turns on the **Allow access to this table via web services** option in Application Access.

What is the outcome of this configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: Users are allowed to write table records but restricts delete via web services.

options.label: B
options.text: Developers from other application scope can write scripts for this table.

options.label: C
options.text: A user having correct permissions, querying via v/eh services can access table records.

options.label: D
options.text: Users querying via web services can access table records, regardless of permissions.

explanation:
This setting permits inbound web-service queries to the table while continuing to enforce the querying user’s required permissions, including applicable access controls.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow: Table design and runtime settings](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/application-development/r_TableApplicationAccessFields.html)

question: What does a workflow context represent?

options.label: A
options.text: The table for which a workflow is defined plus any conditions such as "Active is true"

options.label: B
options.text: It is generated from a workflow version, executes activities, and follows transitions

options.label: C
options.text: The business reason or process for which a workflow is designed

options.label: D
options.text: It is a checked out workflow which is being edited

explanation:
A workflow context is a running workflow instance. It performs the activities and transitions defined by the workflow and retains the runtime state and execution history for that run.

**Learn more:** [Administering workflow contexts](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/legacy-workflow/r_AdministeringWorkflowContexts.html?contentId=IKnM3AsCYmKYXxCcOGrm_w) · [Getting started with workflows](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/servicenow-platform/legacy-workflow/getting-started-workflows.html)

question: Which of the following GlideRecord methods execute a query against a database table? (select 3)
explanation:
GlideRecord `query()` runs the configured query against the table, and `_query()` performs the same operation when a table has a column named `query`. GlideRecord `get()` retrieves a specified record by `sys_id`, display value, or field/value lookup, which queries the table for that record.

**Learn more:** [ServiceNow GlideRecord API — Global](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideRecordAPI.html)

question: When using the Custom UI test step in Automated Test Framework, which of the following is **NOT** a testable page component?
explanation:
